items.review_rationale: Reviewed full arbitrary-space open-set axioms for a family tau of subsets of X, including empty and entire set, closure under arbitrary unions and finite intersections and empty underlying space.

references.context: All subsets of the underlying set X, from which the topology tau is selected.

references.phrase: empty set and whole-set membership in tau
references.context: Axioms that both the empty subset and ambient X are open.
Union over any indexed family of members of the topology, including potentially infinite indexing.
Intersection of any finite collection of open sets, including the empty finite intersection convention.

references.phrase: members of tau are open subsets
references.disposition: Open sets are defined by membership in tau, not imported from metric-space openness or a nonempty-space convention.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed two-sided ideal for a possibly noncommutative associative ring, retaining additive subgroup and both left/right multiplicative absorption as independent conditions.

references.context: Subset closed under addition and additive inverses, containing additive identity, as a subgroup of additive group (R,+).
For every r in R and i in I, product r i remains in I.
For every r in R and i in I, product i r remains in I.

references.phrase: two-sided not merely left or right ideal
references.disposition: Both multiplication directions are required; commutativity is not assumed.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed uniformizer of discrete valuation ring as generator of its maximal ideal, including principal ideal equality and fixed valuation-ring context; not equated with an arbitrary nonunit.

references.context: Smallest ideal containing element pi, equal to all ring multiples pi*a in a commutative ring.

references.phrase: equality of principal ideal (pi) with m
references.context: The maximal ideal is generated by one element pi in the DVR.

references.phrase: uniformizer need not be a unit
references.disposition: A uniformizer generates the proper maximal ideal and is not just any invertible element of A.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed unit of associative unital ring as element possessing a two-sided multiplicative inverse, distinguishing an invertible element from the ring's identity element.

references.context: Two-sided identity for ring multiplication, required to state the unit equations.
Ring element v with uv=1_R and vu=1_R.

references.phrase: a unit need not equal unity
references.disposition: The identity element is itself a unit but most units in a ring need not be the identity.
